what_its_for: Cinacalcet is used to lower high levels of a hormone called PTH (parathyroid hormone) in people who are on dialysis for kidney disease. It is also used to treat high calcium levels in the blood caused by a problem with the parathyroid glands (small glands in your neck). It works by helping your parathyroid glands release less PTH, which helps keep calcium and phosphorus levels balanced in your body.
how_to_take: Take cinacalcet by mouth with food or shortly after eating a meal. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Taking it with food helps your body absorb the medicine better and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your lab results and how well your body responds. The usual starting dose is 30 mg once a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time (up to 180 mg per day) until your calcium and PTH levels are in a healthy range. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is the next day already, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses at once or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store cinacalcet at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it may affect how your body processes the drug. Let your doctor or pharmacist know about all other medicines you take — including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements — because cinacalcet can interact with many other medications, especially antidepressants, antifungals, and heart medicines. Avoid taking calcium supplements, antacids, or phosphate binders without checking with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: muscle cramps, spasms, or twitching; numbness or tingling in your fingers, toes, or around your mouth; seizures; confusion or unusual changes in mood; severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; low blood pressure or dizziness; or if you feel your heart is beating irregularly. These could be signs that your calcium level has dropped too low (a condition called hypocalcemia), which can be serious.
when_it_works: Cinacalcet starts working fairly quickly, and your doctor will check your blood calcium levels within a week of starting or changing your dose. However, it may take several weeks to months for your PTH levels to reach the target range. Regular blood tests are important to make sure the medicine is working safely and effectively for you.
special_populations: Children and teenagers: Cinacalcet is not recommended for children under 18 years of age unless specifically prescribed by a specialist, as it can cause serious low calcium problems in young patients. Older adults: Use with caution; older patients may be more sensitive to side effects. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as the safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk, so talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your dose.
